vulnerability_patterns.description: Unchecked multiplication of horizontal and vertical tile counts could overflow when deriving the total tile count, producing a truncated `dec->numtiles` value that is later used for allocation and indexing logic.
trigger_conditions: Large or malformed image parameters make `dec->numhtiles` and `dec->numvtiles` sufficiently large
The decoder computes `dec->numtiles` via direct multiplication without overflow validation
The resulting `dec->numtiles` is used to size `dec->tiles` or drive subsequent tile-processing loops
fix_patterns: safe API replacement for arithmetic with `jas_safe_size_mul`
explicit overflow guard with early return on failure
compute into `size_t` temporary before assigning the derived count
evidence_lines: Allocation remains `jas_alloc2(dec->numtiles, sizeof(jpc_dec_tile_t))`, showing the checked product feeds allocation sizing

entry_points: decoder setup code in `src/libjasper/jpc/jpc_dec.c` that derives tile grid dimensions
any path computing total element counts from image-controlled width/height/tile geometry
allocation callsites that consume products of dimension/count fields
suggestions: Prioritize products of independently derived dimensions (`count_a * count_b`) that later feed allocation or loop bounds
Prefer missing checked-arithmetic detection over generic allocation-API matching
Track values from image/header fields through `CEILDIV`-style dimension calculations into total-count variables
Flag direct multiplication used as authoritative element count when sibling codebases use helpers like `jas_safe_size_mul`
Look for fix-shape semantics: replacement of raw arithmetic with checked helper plus fail-fast return

analysis_rationale: The patch replaces direct multiplication of tile counts (`dec->numhtiles * dec->numvtiles`) with a checked multiplication helper `jas_safe_size_mul(..., &size)` and aborts on failure. This is concrete evidence that the vulnerable mechanism is unchecked arithmetic overflow in computing the number of tiles before allocation/use, not merely an allocation API change or null-check addition.
